feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: clear positioning, solid career progression, and relevant platform/strategy depth. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on outcome metrics in places, and slightly over-structured with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior profile with consistent progression at NACo, showing increasing scope from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms and tools: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Clarity, automation, and multimedia production.  
- Good writing quality overall: concise, professional tone, and mostly error-free with strong emphasis on governance, systems, and cross-channel leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond activity: include outcomes such as email growth, engagement improvements, traffic gains, cost savings, team size, budget size, or efficiency gains.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve scannability and avoid repetition.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency fixes: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lines); standardize punctuation in bullets and formatting of “French (A2, learning)” instead of “A2/Learning.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, one or two concrete signals of scale, and slightly less repetition of skills listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: e.g., “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years guiding mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations.”
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, large-scale Drupal environments, or analytics/governance leadership.
- Tighten phrasing by replacing “building the workflows and systems that support” with “designing workflows and systems for.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat heavily across Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in multiple NACo roles; keep it, but avoid overemphasizing it here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level strengths will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level phrasing: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS and web platform administration,” “Editorial systems and workflow design.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve scanability; suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS & web platform administration • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Standardize style: use plural “communications” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Consider dropping “Workflow & systems architecture,” which reads vague unless supported by a dedicated systems-focused target role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, editorial systems, analytics, and multimedia.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects section. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant scope, current strategic value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and AI-enabled member discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; start with action + outcome, e.g., “Built cross-channel workflows and analytics systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Separate strategic consulting from hands-on execution: one bullet for governance/operations, one for Drupal microsites/toolkits, one for CMS/front-end troubleshooting, one for AI search.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, teams/users served, launch dates, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, reduced publishing time, or search/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and coordinated communications” repeats the 2022–2024 director entry; frame this as post-tenure consulting/modernization instead.
- Microsite and AI-search details duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and leave project specifics there.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management and video points covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership in one line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management.”
- Prioritize the website transformation as the lead bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused; add performance if available: newsletter growth/open rates, social engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten remaining bullets to distinct executive wins: built first in-house broadcast studio; expanded analytics stack (GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery); formalized governance and publishing standards.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this at a higher strategic level.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries and footer projects; emphasize building institutional capacity, not recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Make it sharper by emphasizing what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + outcome: “Ran NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for county officials nationwide.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: managed 4 weekly newsletters; launched/grew weekly advocacy video; formalized cross-team editorial planning; improved publishing workflow consistency.
- Replace soft phrasing like “helped scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” with direct verbs: “scaled,” “launched,” “standardized,” “streamlined.”
- Add metrics if available: email open/click rates, video views, production volume, publishing turnaround time, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.
- Website/email/social oversight also appears in the 2022–2024 role; keep this entry focused on executional leadership and editorial operations.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and outcomes-oriented strengths most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, differentiated terms: “Enterprise web strategy,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector advocacy communications,” “Audience and content strategy.”
- Consider adding one higher-value capability from recent work, such as “AI-enabled content discovery” or “Analytics-informed content strategy,” to reflect 2022–present impact.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid “focused”/“planning” filler. Example:
- Enterprise web strategy
- Digital governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- AI-enabled content discovery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations”; vary the phrasing or swap in a more distinctive strength.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to a curated, impact-oriented grouping: “Drupal web modernization • CMS migration and governance • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they are already covered in Technical + IT.
- Replace “CMS modernization” with “CMS migration and modernization” if you want clearer alignment to the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.
- Keep only 6–7 items max so the section signals strengths rather than inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; keep here only if it is a target-role differentiator.
- Platform names and coding tools substantially repeat the “Technical + IT” section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads more like a tool list than an impact-oriented topline category. Tighten it to emphasize strategic analytics capability over platform repetition.

- “SEO and performance analysis” is broad; avoid repeating similar wording in recent NACo bullets unless tied to outcomes there.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production environment, delivery scope, and higher-value capabilities rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, more senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ/multi-camera studio systems • Virtual production operations • Post-production editing”

- This largely duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; differentiate or remove one.
- “Studio operations” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” are already implied by NACo experience bullets, so avoid repeating identical wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either sharpen its positioning or be trimmed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize platform administration/implementation, e.g. **CMS & Web Platform Administration**.
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** (Drupal first is right; keep only if all are credible working tools).
- If space allows, add light qualifiers for depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless you want to signal lightweight static-site publishing specifically; it is less aligned with the enterprise/public-sector story.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or differentiating one as “Platforms” and the other as “Technical capabilities.”
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages already appear elsewhere, so this item should not stand alone without clearer purpose.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding terms to applied execution: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers • Deployment automation with GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping versioned/basic terms (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless space allows; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more senior.
- If accurate, add specificity tied to recent work: “Drupal front-end implementation,” “analytics/tag deployment,” or “workflow/deployment automation.”
- Order by relevance/recency: JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless this section is strictly implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more strategic by separating automation tools from collaboration/project platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance to your recent work and automation emphasis: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central to measurable process improvements, reflect that in recent experience bullets instead of here; keep this section concise and tool-focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same concept verbatim in multiple places.
- Slack and Teams are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; current title slightly overstates their function.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational scale already shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal practical ownership of email platforms and audience engagement systems without repeating newsletter details from work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something slightly broader and clearer: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use, not just familiarity: **Campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep it platform-focused; let the work experience carry volume metrics and leadership impact

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered well in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 roles.
- Don’t repeat “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or video updates, audience reach, or production volume.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a full version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve cross-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestream and video content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in 2022–2024 roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project support as the clearest distinct contributions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the most concrete achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the multimedia line and make it outcome-oriented: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast.”
- Add scope if you can: number of episodes, audiences served, stakeholders supported, or types of projects/policy areas.
- Consider a sharper full version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county program and policy work; produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
